transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I asked you to come in because I need to talk to you about your son's visit yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm afraid there was a mistake with the immunizations we gave him. One of the vaccines was drawn up for a child in a higher weight category than your son. This means he received a dose intended for an older, heavier child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is unexpected. I want to be clear that this was a mistake on our part. I am sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that make sense, or can I explain the dosing part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I understand. He got too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. He received a higher dose than what is standard for his weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're worried. It's completely natural to feel concerned when you hear something like this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't want any trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to reassure you that you are not in any trouble, and this has nothing to do with your paperwork or status. We are focusing only on your son's health.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for the confusion this causes. We were very busy in the clinic yesterday, but that doesn't excuse the fact that we didn't double-check the weight band.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Even if it feels fine now, it is still not how we should have handled it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the plan. I have already contacted our pharmacist and the toxicology specialist to determine if there are any specific side effects we need to watch for. I will call you by tomorrow afternoon, Friday, to give you the final word from them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, by 4:00 PM tomorrow. In the meantime, your role is just to monitor him. If you see any unusual rashes or if he seems more lethargic than usual, I want you to call this office immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you have a pen to write down my direct number?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have it in my phone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Great. I will also send a note into his electronic chart so that any other doctor who sees him knows exactly what dose was given.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you might have more questions as you think about this. Do you have any right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. Not really.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: All right. I'll be in touch tomorrow. I really apologize again for the error.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and maintains a steady, non-rushing pace throughout the interaction.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, uses lay language ('too much'), checks comprehension twice, and avoids false reassurance.

A.justification: Direct apologies are used, but the resident includes an excuse regarding the clinic being 'very busy' during the apology process.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('worried') and engages the patient's concern about their status, but only names one specific emotion.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (pharmacist/toxicology), a clear timeline (Friday by 4:00 PM), a patient role (monitor for rashes/lethargy), and prevention (charting for other doctors).
